# M3.md — Material 3, distilled for ii-ren

What Google's Material 3 spec (m3.material.io, M3 Expressive, site version
2026-09-23) says about every part of a UI, with the numbers, mapped onto this
shell's tokens and widgets.

- `DESIGN.md` is the **law**: how this shell does things, and which tokens to use.
- `TASTE.md` is the **owner's taste**: what a surface should be, and calls already made.
- This file is the **reference** those two are built on. Reach for it when the
  law is silent ("what does M3 say a menu item looks like?"), when building a
  component M3 defines, and when auditing a surface against M3.

**Precedence:** an owner's call in `TASTE.md` §9 beats `DESIGN.md`, which beats
this file. Where this shell departs from M3 on purpose it is listed in §1, so an
audit does not "fix" it back.

**Units.** M3 measures in dp. On this shell's one 1080p screen at scale 1, 1dp is
1px. The shell runs denser than M3 (§1), so M3's numbers are the reference
proportions, not literals: take the token from `Appearance` that DESIGN.md maps
them to.

**Anything not here:** `python3 tools/m3-docs.py` mirrors all 88 pages and the
token database to `~/.cache/m3-docs/<version>/` (it prints the path). Then grep:
`pages/<section>__<page>.md`, `tokens/component-<name>.txt`,
`tokens/motion-shape-state.txt`, `tokens/typography.txt`, `tokens/spacing.txt`.

Contents: 1 Departures · 2 Expressive principles · 3 Motion · 4 States and input ·
5 Colour · 6 Typography · 7 Shape · 8 Spacing and layout · 9 Elevation ·
10 Icons · 11 Components · 12 Writing · 13 Accessibility · 14 Refreshing

## 1. Where this shell departs from M3

### 1.1 Decided — do not "fix"

| Topic | M3 says | This shell | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Density | 48dp touch / 44dp pointer targets; density is opt-in | 32px minimum hit area, 40 where a mis-click costs; rows 40–56; compact buttons 30. Roughly M3 density −2 (each step −4dp of height) | DESIGN 3.4, 5.2 |
| Type scale | 15 sp styles, Major Second from 14 | its own px scale, mapped in §6.1 | DESIGN 7 |
| Corner scale | 4/8/12/16/20/28/32/48dp | its own px values (8/12/17/23/30) | DESIGN 4.1 |
| Enter/exit of anchored surfaces | Android components "expand and collapse along the x or y axis; scale is avoided" | anchored popups pop on `ArrowPopupMotion` (scale 0.5 → 1.02 → 1, from the opener's corner), as Launcher3 does | TASTE 5.3, §9 |
| Dividers | full-width/inset dividers, menu and list dividers allowed | none, anywhere. Whitespace and container tone only | DESIGN 5.5, TASTE 2.10 |
| Overscroll | Android stretch | none | DESIGN 3.6, TASTE §9 |
| Disabled | content onSurface @0.38, container onSurface @0.10, no state layers | `opacity: 0.4` on the whole control | DESIGN 3.1 |
| Notifications | one joined, segmented stack | separate `rounding.large` cards, 8 apart | TASTE §9 |
| Dock icons | ripple | hover scale 1.1, press squish 0.88, no ripple (Launcher3) | DESIGN 3.3 |
| Hand cursor | links and clickable images only | every clickable | DESIGN 3.4 |

### 1.2 Open — differs from M3, not yet decided by the owner

Do not change these piecemeal; they need one decision each.

1. **Effects curves.** M3's own spring→curve table gives each effects speed its
   own curve: fast `0.31, 0.94, 0.34, 1.00` @150ms, default `0.34, 0.80, 0.34, 1.00`
   @200ms, slow `0.34, 0.88, 0.34, 1.00` @300ms. `Appearance` uses the default
   curve for all three, at 130/200/280ms. Fixing it retimes every exit in the
   shell, and the owner declined a motion pass on 2026-09-27 (TASTE §9).
2. **Scrim.** M3: the scrim role at 32% opacity. `colScrim` is 50%.
3. **Keyboard focus ring.** M3 draws a 3dp ring in `secondary`, 2dp outside the
   control, on keyboard focus. The ii family draws only the 0.10 focus layer.
4. **Tooltip linger.** M3 hides a tooltip 1.5s after the pointer leaves.
   `StyledToolTip` hides at once.

## 2. M3 Expressive in one page

Expressive is a set of tactics for steering attention, backed by eye-tracking
research: people found key elements up to four times faster. The tactics:

- **Colour and contrast.** The primary role on the one action that matters;
  secondary for supporting ones; contrasting hues rather than near-identical ones.
- **Containment and grouping.** Related things in subtle containers; sections
  separated by space, containers and headings.
- **Size.** The most important action is the largest element on the surface.
- **Shape and shape morph.** Shape adds emphasis, guides focus, tells containers
  and buttons apart; morph shows state (selected, pressed), progress, or change.
- **Typography.** Emphasized styles for the key text; larger type for the
  primary action.
- **Motion.** Emphasizes key moments. Use it sparingly — it distracts.

Rules that come with them:

1. **Design for the primary goal.** One primary task per surface, made obvious by
   size, colour and placement; secondary and tertiary goals use fewer tactics.
2. **Don't stack tactics.** Several expressive tactics at once distract. A
   secondary surface (a report, a settings page) gets fewer, not more.
3. **Calm, balanced layouts.** Uniform shapes and sizes in a set, even spacing,
   consistent alignment. Text that changes width while something else animates
   is a caution in M3's own example.
4. **Shape is versatile, not semantic.** A wave is not "progress"; don't assign
   a meaning to one shape.
5. **Abstract shapes sparingly**, on imagery and decoration — never on a
   text-heavy container.
6. **Tension is allowed.** Mixing square and round on purpose (selected vs
   unselected, a hero element) is expressive; mixing them by accident is noise.

This is TASTE.md §2 in Google's words: one primary action, one loud thing.

## 3. Motion

### 3.1 The physics system

Since M3 Expressive (May 2025) motion is **springs**, not easing curves. A spring
is stiffness + damping (+ initial velocity); it handles interruption, retargeting
and gestures without special cases. There are two **schemes** — *expressive*
(Material's default: overshoots and settles, for most products and every hero
moment) and *standard* (minimal bounce, for utilitarian products) — each with
three speeds of two kinds:

- **Spatial** — position, size, rotation, corner radius. Overshoots.
- **Effects** — colour, opacity. Never overshoots.

| Token `md.sys.motion.spring.*` | Expressive ζ / stiffness | Standard ζ / stiffness | M3's curve for non-spring platforms | Shell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fast.spatial` | 0.6 / 800 | 0.9 / 1400 | exp `0.42, 1.67, 0.21, 0.90` 350ms · std `0.27, 1.06, 0.18, 1.00` 350ms | `elementMoveSmall`, `elementResize`, `clickBounce` |
| `default.spatial` | 0.8 / 380 | 0.9 / 700 | exp `0.38, 1.21, 0.22, 1.00` 500ms · std `0.27, 1.06, 0.18, 1.00` 500ms | `elementMove`, `elementMoveEnter` |
| `slow.spatial` | 0.8 / 200 | 0.9 / 300 | exp `0.39, 1.29, 0.35, 0.98` 650ms · std `0.27, 1.06, 0.18, 1.00` 750ms | `expressiveSlowSpatial` |
| `fast.effects` | 1.0 / 3800 | 1.0 / 3800 | `0.31, 0.94, 0.34, 1.00` 150ms | `elementMoveExit` (§1.2) |
| `default.effects` | 1.0 / 1600 | 1.0 / 1600 | `0.34, 0.80, 0.34, 1.00` 200ms | `elementMoveFast` |
| `slow.effects` | 1.0 / 800 | 1.0 / 800 | `0.34, 0.88, 0.34, 1.00` 300ms | `expressiveSlowEffectsDuration` (§1.2) |

Which speed (M3's own examples):

| Speed | Spatial | Effects |
|---|---|---|
| fast | small components: switches, buttons | colour change of a switch handle |
| default | things covering part of the screen: a sheet, an expanded rail | opacity of the content inside a rail |
| slow | full-screen motion | a full-screen content refresh |

"All component motion is driven by two tokens: expressive fast spatial and
expressive fast effects." A component reacting to input is almost always fast.

Schemes can be swapped per element: expressive for most of the product, standard
for a moment that should not feel playful (a destructive confirmation, an
error). The split button's menu chevron rotates on the standard scheme even in
an expressive product.

### 3.2 Easing and duration — still the system for transitions

M3 marks easing+duration as legacy for components but **still uses it for
transitions** (surfaces and screens moving on a fixed trip). Suggested pairs:

| Easing | Duration | Transition |
|---|---|---|
| emphasized | 500ms | begins and ends on screen |
| emphasized decelerate | 400ms | enters the screen |
| emphasized accelerate | 200ms | exits the screen |
| standard | 300ms | begins and ends on screen, small/utility |
| standard decelerate | 250ms | enters, small/utility |
| standard accelerate | 200ms | exits, small/utility |

Curves (`Appearance.animationCurves.*`): emphasized =
`M 0,0 C 0.05,0 0.133333,0.06 0.166666,0.4 C 0.208333,0.82 0.25,1 1,1`;
emphasizedDecel `0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1`; emphasizedAccel `0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15`;
standard `0.2, 0, 0, 1`; standardDecel `0, 0, 0, 1`; standardAccel `0.3, 0, 1, 1`.
Legacy (M2) `0.4, 0, 0.2, 1` — never use it.

Choosing the easing by what the surface does relative to the screen:

- **Begins and ends on screen** → emphasized.
- **Enters** → emphasized decelerate: starts at peak velocity, lands gently.
- **Exits permanently** (dismissed, gone) → emphasized accelerate: ends at peak
  velocity, which reads as "cannot be retrieved".
- **Exits temporarily** (a drawer or sidebar that will come back) → emphasized,
  coming to rest just off screen, which reads as "still there".

Choosing the duration: scale it with the **area the transition covers** (200ms
for a radio button, 500ms for an album taking over the screen), and make
**exits shorter than enters** — the user has already moved on. Durations above
600ms are for ambient motion with no user input (a carousel auto-advancing:
1000ms emphasized). Ladder: short 50/100/150/200, medium 250/300/350/400,
long 450/500/550/600, extra-long 700/800/900/1000.

### 3.3 The six transition patterns

| Pattern | Use for | Motion | In this shell |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Container transform** | an element becoming the detail it opens: card → page, FAB → sheet, search box → results | a persistent container morphs from start to end state; the strongest relationship, the most expressive | a control expanding into the surface it opens. Reserve for hero moments; it is excessive for deep or frequent navigation |
| **Forward and backward** | consecutive levels of hierarchy: list → item | Android: horizontal slide **with a fade**, so screens need not travel full width | settings sub-pages, a thread → its message |
| **Lateral** | peers at one level: tabs, carousels, galleries | grouped elements slide in unison, **no fade** (a fade makes it read as forward/back) | sidebar tabs, cheatsheet pages |
| **Top level** | destinations of a nav rail/bar/drawer | exiting screen fades out quickly, then the new one fades in; no slide, no shared element | settings nav-rail pages |
| **Enter and exit** | a component appearing within the screen (dialog, menu, snackbar, tooltip) or crossing its edge (sheet, drawer, bar) | Android: expands/collapses along x or y, away from the edge it belongs to (a top menu grows down, a bottom snackbar grows up); beyond-bounds surfaces slide in from their own edge | popups (but see §1.1), sidebars, the bar's reveal |
| **Skeleton loader** | loading → loaded | subtle pulse moving top-left to bottom-right; content fades in quickly on top | held-size tiles while images load (TASTE 4.1) |

Spatial model: a surface enters from where it lives. Notifications from the top
(that is where their drawer is), a drawer from its side, a sheet or keyboard
from the bottom.

Don'ts: a lateral slide for hierarchy (too much motion, implies peers); a
lateral slide between top-level destinations (conflicts with swipeable content);
an enter/exit sheet slide for hierarchy navigation; container transform in deep
utility hierarchies (settings) — use forward/backward.

### 3.4 What makes a transition good

- **Follows reduced-motion settings.** With reduced motion: subtle fades instead
  of slides and scales; parallax and shape morph off. (Here: `animationMultiplier`
  ≤ 0.25 is "off", DESIGN 2.9.)
- **Consistent.** The same kind of move uses the same pattern everywhere.
- **Stable layout.** Nothing pops in and shifts; skeletons hold the space.
- **No jump cuts** — except that dense desktop menus *may* open instantly when
  efficiency is the point.
- **Coherent spatial model.** Don't switch axes between collapsed and expanded.
- **Unified direction.** Elements move together along one primary axis; only a
  hero element stays persistent. Many parts moving independently is a don't.
- **Clean fades.** Fade the old content fully out before fading the new in. If a
  crossfade is unavoidable, keep it short and hide it in the fastest part of the
  motion. Never slowly fade a sheet or panel over content — that is the
  "transparent sheet" don't.
- **Simple style.** "Common transitions should not use overt style effects like
  bouncy springs." Bounce belongs to components reacting to input, not to a
  surface on a routine trip (DESIGN 2.4).

### 3.5 Component motion, per M3

- **Buttons, icon buttons:** pressed shape morphs toward square on the fast
  spatial spring; toggles morph round ↔ square when selected (§7.3).
- **Standard button group:** the pressed button widens and its neighbours
  narrow, briefly. **Connected group:** only the pressed button's shape changes.
- **Split button:** the trailing chevron rotates 180° inward, on the *standard*
  scheme, and its inner corners morph.
- **Switch:** handle 16dp (off) → 24dp (on) → 28dp while pressed, sliding to the
  other end.
- **Slider:** the 4dp handle narrows while pressed or dragged; the value label
  appears.
- **Navigation rail/bar:** the active indicator expands from the icon's centre,
  along one axis only; the icon fills.
- **FAB:** appears by expanding from its centre. A FAB menu's close button takes
  the FAB's place and items enter from the FAB's top trailing corner. Extended
  FAB ↔ FAB on scroll: the shape changes, the icon moves, the label fades.
- **Menus:** enter/exit from the trigger; the trigger shows a pressed state
  while its menu is open; filtered items ease to their new places.
- **Tooltips:** fade in on hover (or focus); gone 1.5s after leaving; one at a time.
- **Snackbar:** one at a time; nothing else animates along with it.
- **Loading indicator:** a looping morph through seven Material shapes.
- **Progress:** linear runs leading → trailing, circular clockwise from the top;
  determinate starts as a dot; indeterminate grows and shrinks along the track.
- **Carousel:** items resize as they move and snap on release; images parallax.
- **Lists:** expand via container transform; a selected item's corners morph.
- **Search bar:** widens on focus (side margins 24 → 12).
- **Cards:** picked up → elevation rises; a dragged card never bumps others.
- **Shape morph** uses the expressive scheme by default.

## 4. States and input

### 4.1 State layers

A state layer is a translucent overlay **in the content colour** (the `on-`
colour of the container) between container and content. Fixed opacities
(`md.sys.state.*`): **hover 0.08, focus 0.10, pressed 0.10, dragged 0.16**;
disabled content 0.38.

- Only **one state layer at a time** per element; states combine (hovered +
  selected, focused + selected) but the layer shows the current interaction.
- The layer is 40dp where the target is 48dp; it can cover the whole component,
  a part, or a circle over part of it.
- Hover appears and disappears with a low-emphasis animated fade.
- There is only ever one hovered, one focused, one pressed and one dragged
  element in a layout.
- The layer is always the content (icon or label) colour, also when a component
  is remapped to non-default colours.

In this shell: `colLayerNHover`/`colLayerNActive`, `StateOverlay`, `StateLayer`
(DESIGN 3.1).

### 4.2 Who takes which state

| State | Inherited by | Not by (their *items* take it instead) |
|---|---|---|
| Hover | buttons, cards, checkbox, chips, pickers, list items, slider, switch, text fields | app bars, badges, dialogs, menus, nav bar/rail/drawer, sheets, tabs |
| Focus | buttons, cards, checkbox, chips, pickers, list items, selection controls, text fields | app bars, badges, banners, dialogs, nav bar/rail/drawer, sheets |
| Pressed (ripple) | buttons, cards, checkbox, chips, list items, text fields | app bars, badges, dialogs, menus, sheets, tabs |
| Dragged | cards, chips, list items, sliders | app bars, badges, buttons, dialogs, menus, navigation |
| Disabled | buttons, cards, checkboxes, chips, list items, radios, switches, text fields | app bars, badges, dialogs, FABs, menus, navigation, sheets, tabs, tooltips |

So a whole panel, bar, menu or dialog never lights up on hover — the things in
it do. **Pressed** may add elevation (buttons, cards). **Dragged** is low
emphasis: the 0.16 layer plus a lift (list item and chip dragged elevation is
level 4).

### 4.3 Disabled

- Disabled components can't be focused, pressed or dragged and don't react to
  hover. Exception: a **disabled menu item still takes focus** (it is announced,
  just not selectable).
- Disabled does not need to meet contrast.
- Show a menu item disabled rather than removing it when it is only sometimes
  available. A **FAB is never disabled** — if its action is unavailable it is
  not shown. A dialog's **dismissive action is never disabled**; its confirming
  action is disabled until a choice is made.
- This shell: `opacity: 0.4` on the whole control (§1.1); dim once (TASTE 3.6).

### 4.4 Selection

- Show selection with **at least two cues, never colour alone**: filled icon (or
  semibold weight if no filled glyph), checkmark, shape change, plus colour.
- Navigation components and tabs show the current destination with an **active
  indicator**, and only one item has it.
- Desktop: when selection is the main task, checkboxes are always visible; when
  it is secondary, a checkbox appears on hover, then on every item once one is
  selected.
- Toggle icon buttons go outlined → filled when selected (weight → semibold if
  there is no filled glyph). Don't use a toggle for something with no selected
  state (an overflow button).

### 4.5 Keyboard

- **Tab / Shift+Tab** move between components in reading order (left → right,
  top → bottom). **Arrow keys** move *inside* a component: button groups,
  lists, menus, tabs, radio groups, chip sets, carousels, segmented controls.
  **Space / Enter** activate. **Home / End** jump to ends (sliders).
- **Escape** dismisses any modal surface (menu, dialog, sheet), removes the
  focus indicator, and in a text field drops the caret **without** clearing the
  typed text.
- **Initial focus:** a dialog → its first interactive element, with Tab cycling
  inside it; a menu → its first item; a FAB menu → the close button; a radio
  group → the selected radio; a list → the selected item or the first; a
  carousel → the first item, never the container; a button group → the first
  button, never the container.
- **Return focus** to the element that opened a dialog or menu when it closes.
- **Keyboard focus indicator:** a ring, 3dp thick (`md.sys.state.focus-indicator.thickness`),
  2dp outside the control (`outer-offset`), in `secondary`; menu items use the
  inner offset (−3dp). See §1.2.3.
- **Shortcuts** use two or more keys. A single-key shortcut is only acceptable
  while its component has focus. Document custom shortcuts (here: the cheatsheet).

### 4.6 Pointer

- Primary click gives the same feedback as touch (the ripple).
- **Secondary click opens a context menu** for the object under the cursor.
- Cursors: pointer by default; hand on links and linked images (this shell uses
  it on every clickable, §1.1); resize arrows on resizable edges; I-beam on text.
- Text: single click places the caret, double selects a word, triple a paragraph;
  selection is one flat colour.
- The wheel scrolls the thing under the cursor, only; a horizontal list must
  scroll from the wheel too.
- Hover should also reveal tooltips where applicable.

### 4.7 Gestures and their single-pointer alternative

Long press selects or picks up; drag reorders or moves surfaces; swipe switches
peers or acts on an item. **Every drag or swipe action needs a single-pointer
alternative** — a menu entry, a button. A card or list item carries one swipe
action at most, and content that itself swipes (a carousel) is not put inside
something swipeable.

### 4.8 Targets

48×48dp for touch, **44×44dp for pointers**, targets 8dp apart. The target can
be larger than the visual (a 24dp icon in a 48dp target). This shell: 32/40,
§1.1.

## 5. Colour

### 5.1 How the scheme is made

A source colour (here: the wallpaper, quantised) → five key colours (primary,
secondary, tertiary, neutral, neutral variant) → a tonal palette of each (tones
0–100, plus 95/98/99) → tones assigned to the colour roles for light and dark,
at standard, medium (3:1) or high (7:1) contrast. Colours are reasoned about in
**HCT** (hue, chroma, tone); tone alone decides contrast, so never mix HSL
lightness into it.

This shell: `scripts/colors/generate_colors_material.py` (materialyoucolor),
scheme from `Config.options.appearance.palette.type` (`auto` picks neutral or
tonal spot by the wallpaper's colourfulness), standard contrast. `success` is a
**static custom role** (M3's "define static colours"), deliberately not
harmonised; terminal colours are harmonised toward primary.

### 5.2 The roles

| Role | For | Shell |
|---|---|---|
| primary / on primary | the highest-emphasis fills, text, icons: the FAB, a filled button, an active state | `colPrimary` / `colOnPrimary` |
| primary container / on | a standout fill for key components | `colPrimaryContainer` / `colOnPrimaryContainer` |
| secondary / on | less prominent fills, text, icons | `colSecondary` / `colOnSecondary` |
| secondary container / on | recessive fills: tonal buttons, selected nav item, filter chips | `colSecondaryContainer` / `colOnSecondaryContainer` |
| tertiary (+container) | contrasting accents that balance primary/secondary; badges, input emphasis; vibrant menus | `colTertiary`, `colTertiaryContainer`, `colOnTertiary*` |
| error (+container) | errors only; static even in dynamic schemes | `colError`, `colOnError`, `colErrorContainer`, `colOnErrorContainer` |
| surface | default background | `colLayer0` |
| surface container lowest → highest | containers, from least to most emphasis | `m3colors.m3surfaceContainerLowest`, `colLayer1`…`colLayer4` = `colSurfaceContainerLow`…`Highest` |
| on surface | text and icons on any surface | `colOnSurface` (= `colOnLayer2..4`) |
| on surface variant | lower-emphasis text and icons | `colOnSurfaceVariant` (= `colOnLayer1`) |
| outline | important boundaries: text field outline, a control's edge | `colOutline` |
| outline variant | decorative edges, and borders of controls whose contents already give contrast | `colOutlineVariant` |
| inverse surface / on / primary | reversed elements: snackbar, plain tooltip, and the action in them | `colTooltip` / `colOnTooltip` / `m3colors.m3inversePrimary` |
| scrim | dimming behind modals | `colScrim` (§1.2.2) |
| surface dim / bright | keep their relative brightness in both themes | `m3colors.m3surfaceDim` / `m3surfaceBright` |
| primary/secondary/tertiary fixed (+dim, on, on variant) | same tone in light and dark | `m3colors.m3primaryFixed`… |

Use the semantic `col*` token when one exists (DESIGN 6.1); the roles with no
semantic token are read from `m3colors`.

### 5.3 Rules

1. **Pair as designed.** Text and icons on X use on-X. A container role is never
   text or an icon colour. Any `on-` pair meets 4.5:1; other pairs may not.
2. **Accent by importance.** Primary for the most important element, secondary
   for what doesn't need immediate attention (the selected nav icon's
   background, a dismissive button), tertiary for small things that need special
   emphasis (a badge). One loud thing (TASTE 2.3).
3. **Surface containers nest by emphasis**, and a container on a container must
   be **more than one step apart** to stay visible (a search bar is
   `surfaceContainerHigh` and must not sit on `surfaceContainer`).
4. **Outline vs outline variant.** Outline for important boundaries and the edge
   of a control that must be found; outline variant for decoration. Never outline
   variant as the only edge of a target — unless the target's content already
   gives contrast.
5. **Fixed colours** don't flip between themes, so they break contrast easily.
   Use them only where contrast isn't needed.
6. **Error stays error.** Don't replace semantic colours (red error, green
   success) with dynamic or content-based colour.
7. **Content-based colour** (a scheme from album art): only in a contained area
   next to its source, with the source visible; at most two schemes on one
   screen.
8. **Elevation is tone, not tint.** Surface tint is deprecated; surfaces at
   different heights use different surface-container roles.
9. **Contrast:** small text 4.5:1, large text (≥14pt bold / 18pt) 3:1, controls
   in a cluster 3:1 against the background, selected vs unselected menu items
   3:1. Disabled is exempt. Standalone prominent controls (a FAB) needn't hit 3:1
   container-to-background.
10. **Default text** is on surface; on surface variant is the strong alternative.
    Links are primary (tertiary to be quieter) **and underlined**.

## 6. Typography

### 6.1 The scale

30 styles: 15 baseline + 15 emphasized (same size and line height, heavier).
Sizes in sp; Major Second (1.125) from a 14 base. Baseline weights: regular 400,
medium 500; emphasized: 500 or bold 700.

| Style | Size / line | Baseline wght | Emphasized wght | Nearest shell token |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| display large | 57 / 64 | 400 | 500 | — |
| display medium | 45 / 52 | 400 | 500 | — |
| display small | 36 / 44 | 400 | 500 | `display` (36) |
| headline large | 32 / 40 | 400 | 500 | — |
| headline medium | 28 / 36 | 400 | 500 | — |
| headline small | 24 / 32 | 400 | 500 | `hugeass` (23) |
| title large | 22 / 28 | 400 | 500 | `huge` (22) |
| title medium | 16 / 24 | 500 | 700 | `normal` (16), title family |
| title small | 14 / 20 | 500 | 700 | `small` (15), title family |
| body large | 16 / 24 | 400 | 500 | `normal` (16) |
| body medium | 14 / 20 | 400 | 500 | `small` (15) |
| body small | 12 / 16 | 400 | 500 | `smaller` (12) |
| label large | 14 / 20 | 500 | 700 | `smallie` (13) – `small` (15) |
| label medium | 12 / 16 | 500 | 700 | `smaller` (12) |
| label small | 11 / 16 | 500 | 700 | `smallest` (10) |

Tracking is 0 in the variable-font scale; the static Roboto scale adds 0.1–0.5
on body and label styles.

### 6.2 Which style where

- **Display** — short, important text or numerals; one per page (a greeting, a
  clock). The place for an expressive face.
- **Headline** — short high-emphasis text, a dialog's title (headline small).
- **Title** — medium emphasis, section heads, an app bar's title (title large),
  tabs (title small).
- **Body** — longer passages. No decorative faces.
- **Label** — text inside components, captions, timecodes.

Component text, per the tokens: buttons XS/S **label large**, M **title medium**,
L headline small, XL headline large · extended FAB S title medium, M title
large · chips label large · list item label **body large**, supporting body
medium, trailing/overline label small · menu item **label large**, supporting
body small · dialog headline **headline small**, body **body medium**, actions
label large · plain tooltip **body small**; rich tooltip subhead title small,
body body medium · snackbar body medium, action label large · text field input
body large, floated label and supporting text body small · tabs title small ·
nav rail/bar item label medium (horizontal rail item label large) · badge label
small · slider value label large · search input body large.

### 6.3 Emphasized styles

For **selection, unread items, the primary action, headlines** — anything whose
state or importance should read in the type itself. Swap the baseline style for
the emphasized one of the same size; don't jump a size. Components don't use
them by default. This shell has one heavier weight token: `variableAxes.title`
(wght 550) over `main`'s 450 — use it, don't invent a third.

### 6.4 Rules

- **Brand vs plain face.** Large styles (display, headline) may use the brand
  face for expression; body and label use the plain face for legibility. Here:
  `font.family.title` / `expressive` vs `main`.
- **Line height** ≈ 1.2× size for title and up, ≈ 1.5× for body and label.
- **Tabular figures** for anything that changes or aligns in columns — clocks,
  counters, percentages: `font.family.numbers`.
- **Never shrink type to fit.** Wrap (or elide with a way to see the rest:
  tooltip, expansion). Button, chip and nav labels never wrap; nav labels never
  truncate.
- **Variable axes:** very light weights fail on low-resolution screens at small
  sizes; excessive weight at small sizes hurts too. Light-on-dark text looks
  heavier — a negative grade compensates. Match optical size to the size used.
- **Don't change sizes** when customising a scale; change faces, line height,
  tracking. Avoid styles that differ by a step too small to read as different.
- Supports text at 200% with padding unchanged (§8.6).

---

## 7. Shape

### 7.1 Corner scale

| M3 token | dp | Shell (`Appearance.rounding`) |
|---|---|---|
| none | 0 | 0 |
| extra small | 4 | `unsharpenmore` (6) |
| small | 8 | `verysmall` (8) |
| medium | 12 | `small` (12) |
| large | 16 | `normal` (17) |
| large increased | 20 | — |
| extra large | 28 | `large` (23) |
| extra large increased | 32 | `verylarge` (30) |
| extra extra large | 48 | — |
| full | pill/circle | `full` |

Components map to a step, not a number: buttons full, cards medium (12), chips
small (8), dialogs extra large (28), menus large (16, expressive), FAB large (16)
/ medium FAB 20 / large FAB 28, side sheets large on the free edge, text field
(filled) extra small on the top corners only.

### 7.2 Rules

- **Optical roundness:** inner radius = outer radius − padding between them
  (48 − 14 = 34). Equal radii on nested shapes look unbalanced (DESIGN 4.2).
- **Asymmetric "inner corners"** for closely grouped items — menus, split
  buttons, connected button groups, segmented lists: the outer corners follow the
  group's radius, the corners facing a neighbour are small (§7.3).
- Don't put large or full corners on information-dense containers (cards of
  text); cut corners clip content more than round ones and need padding.
- Abstract library shapes on imagery, avatars, decoration, loading — never on
  text-heavy containers (§2).

### 7.3 Morph values, from the tokens

**Buttons and icon buttons** (pressed morph on the fast spatial spring):

| Size | Height | Resting square | Pressed | Selected (from round) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| XS | 32 | 12 | 8 | 12 |
| S | 40 | 12 | 8 | 12 |
| M | 56 | 16 | 12 | 16 |
| L | 96 | 28 | 16 | 28 |
| XL | 136 | 28 | 16 | 28 |

Round and square buttons share the pressed shape. A selected toggle goes round →
square, or square → round if it rests square. (DESIGN 4.3: opt in per widget;
never on pills that are really pills.)

**Connected button group / split button inner corners:** 2dp gap; inner radius
XS 4, S 8, M 8, L 16, XL 20 (split button inner: 4/4/4/8/12).

**Expressive list items:** resting 4 (16 on the group's outer corners), hovered
12, focused/pressed/dragged/selected 16; segmented gap 2dp.

**Expressive menus:** container 16 (an inactive submenu 8); items 4, the first
and last item's outer corners 12, selected item 12; groups 8 with 2dp padding
and 2dp gaps.

---

## 8. Spacing and layout

### 8.1 Tokens

`md.sys.measurement.space*`, base 8dp (`space100`):

| 0 | 25 | 50 | 75 | 100 | 125 | 150 | 175 | 200 | 250 | 300 | 400 | 450 | 500 | 600 | 700 | 800 | 900 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 20 | 24 | 32 | 36 | 40 | 48 | 56 | 64 | 72 |

2, 6, 10 and 14 are M3's own "nested units". New ones follow the multiplier
(`space225` = 18). This shell writes them as literals on the grid (DESIGN 5.1).

### 8.2 Padding, gaps, margins

- **Padding** is inside an element; **gaps** are between elements in a
  container; **margins** are outside. Define padding and gaps **on the parent**;
  margins on children are rarely uniform and are a smell.
- Simple components have one horizontal and one vertical gap; complex ones name
  gaps by what is on each side ("icon–label gap").
- Use leading/trailing, not left/right, in names and thinking — they swap in RTL.

### 8.3 Grouping and attention

- **Explicit grouping:** containers, outlines, shadows. **Implicit:** proximity
  and space. This shell uses containers and space, never lines.
- **Rhythm:** consistent spacing between related items. **Similarity:** like
  things share size and spacing; leading elements (icons, thumbnails) align.
  **Proximity:** controls sit next to what they affect. **Continuity:** a row of
  chips reads as one control.
- **Emphasis:** generous space and the brightest surface around the most
  important content; negative space gives it form.

### 8.4 Density

Opt-in only, never the default. A step is −4dp of height (vertical padding).
Text size never changes with density. Never densify focused tasks (a menu) or
alerts (dialogs, snackbars).

### 8.5 Line length

40–60 characters is ideal; up to 120 on large screens, with more line height.
Widen margins or split into columns rather than stretch text.

### 8.6 Text scaling

At up to 200% text, text and line height scale; padding and gaps don't.
Components without text don't resize. Reflow (stack side-by-side buttons),
grow containers, scroll vertically — never clip.

---

## 9. Elevation

| Level | dp | Resting for (M3) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | filled/tonal/outlined buttons, button groups, filled/outlined cards, chips, icon buttons, lists, nav rail, segmented, docked side sheet, slider, split button, tabs, unscrolled app bar, a FAB inside a rail |
| 1 | 1 | elevated button/card/chip, modal bottom/side sheet, modal drawer, banner |
| 2 | 3 | **menus**, nav bar, rich tooltip, toolbar, scrolled app bar |
| 3 | 6 | **dialogs**, FAB, extended FAB, search, date/time pickers, floating toolbar |
| 4 | 8 | never resting: hover and drag states (a dragged chip or list item) |
| 5 | 12 | never resting |

- Hover raises a component **one level** (a FAB 3 → 4; buttons +1). Elevation
  changes respond to interaction or system events, consistently.
- Shadows only to **protect** an element on a busy background or to **encourage
  interaction** (lift on drag). By default, separation is tone.
- Scrims sit under modals and expanded navigation: the scrim role at **32%**
  (§1.2.2).
- Any overlapping containment areas need different colour roles.

---

## 10. Icons

Material Symbols, Rounded style here (`font.family.iconMaterial`), through
`MaterialSymbol`. Four axes:

- **Weight** 100–700; 400 matches regular text. Not below 200 at 24dp; don't
  mix weights in one set.
- **Fill** 0–1: outlined → filled is how selection reads. Default (non-toggle)
  icon buttons and the FAB use filled icons; toggles go outlined → filled; with
  no filled glyph, semibold.
- **Grade** for fine thickness without changing size: −25 for light icons on
  dark backgrounds, positive for an emphasized active state. (`MaterialSymbol`
  leaves `GRAD` at 0.)
- **Optical size** 20–48, matched to the rendered size (`MaterialSymbol` does
  this from `iconSize`).

Sizes: **20** for dense/desktop layouts, **24** standard, **40–48** for display
or primary emphasis. Next to text: same size as the text, same optical weight,
baseline shifted down ≈11.5% of the text size.

An icon-only control describes its **action** in a tooltip ("Add to
favourites", not "heart"). Abstract icons need labels; navigation items always
have them. Under 20dp, complex or key-action icons need a text label.

---

## 11. Components

Each entry: what M3 specifies, then the widget that does it here. Sizes are M3's
dp; scale them to the shell's density through `Appearance` (§1.1).

### 11.1 Choosing an action component

| Emphasis | Component | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| highest | FAB, extended FAB, FAB menu | the screen's primary constructive action (create, compose) |
| high | filled button | the final or unblocking step: Save, Confirm, Done |
| high | split button | a key action with variants (Send / schedule send) |
| high | standard button group | several key actions with interplay (back, play, next) |
| medium | tonal button | supporting actions, or a final action that should be calmer |
| medium | elevated button | only where a busy background needs separation |
| medium | outlined button | important but not primary; "change your mind / escape" |
| low | connected button group | choosing among related options that change the view |
| low | text button | optional actions: Learn more, View all; dialog actions |
| low | icon button | compact supplementary actions |

One high-emphasis button per screen. Buttons side by side, not stacked, when
there is room. No more than three buttons in one arrangement — beyond that,
chips, an overflow menu or icon buttons.

### 11.2 Buttons — `RippleButton`, `RippleButtonWithIcon`, `DialogButton`, `GroupButton`

| Size | Height | Side padding | Icon | Icon–label gap | Label | Outline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| XS | 32 | 12 | 20 | 4 | label large | 1 |
| S (default) | 40 | 16 | 20 | 8 | label large | 1 |
| M | 56 | 24 | 24 | 8 | title medium | 1 |
| L | 96 | 48 | 32 | 12 | headline small | 2 |
| XL | 136 | 64 | 40 | 16 | headline large | 3 |

Shapes and morphs: §7.3. Colours (default / toggle unselected / toggle selected):

| Style | Container / content | Shell |
|---|---|---|
| filled | primary / on primary · surface container / on surface variant · primary / on primary | `colPrimary`, `colOnPrimary` (+`Hover`/`Active`) |
| tonal | secondary container / on secondary container · same · secondary / on secondary | `colSecondaryContainer` (+`Hover`/`Active`) |
| elevated | surface container low / primary, elevation 1 (hover 2) · … · primary / on primary | `colSurfaceContainerLow` + shadow |
| outlined | transparent, outline variant edge / on surface variant · … · inverse surface / inverse on surface | `colOutlineVariant` border |
| text | transparent / primary; no toggle | `colLayerNHover` film, `colPrimary` text |

Rules: label 1–3 words, sentence case, one line, never truncated, never
narrower than its label; icon leading, never two icons, icon and label stay
grouped and centred; width hugs the label (or fills responsively, but never
long and flat); filled at most once per page; outlined looks like a chip —
don't put them next to chips; text buttons are never underlined; toggle labels
keep a similar length in both states. Elevated only on busy backgrounds.

### 11.3 Icon buttons — `RippleButton` (square), `IconToolbarButton`, `ToolbarButton`

Sizes XS 32 / S 40 / M 56 / L 96 / XL 136 with icon 20/24/24/32/40. Three
widths by side padding — XS 4/6/10, S 4/8/14, M 12/16/24, L 16/32/48, XL
32/48/72 (narrow/default/wide). Colours: filled (primary), tonal (secondary
container), outlined (outline variant edge, on surface variant), **standard**
(no container, on surface variant; primary when selected). Filled sparingly;
standard on colourful surfaces. Same importance → same size; the main action
(play/pause) is the largest. Tooltip with the action on hover. Toggle: outlined
→ filled icon (or semibold), round → square.

### 11.4 Button groups — `ButtonGroup` + `GroupButton` (standard); `SelectionGroupButton` (connected)

- **Standard:** invisible container, padding between buttons by size — XS 18,
  S 12, M/L/XL 8 — so buttons can animate width and shape without moving the
  layout. Pressing widens the button and squeezes its neighbours. Same size and
  shape throughout; mix width and colour, not shape (except a selected
  button). Hugs its buttons.
- **Connected** (replaces segmented buttons): 2dp between buttons, inner corners
  per §7.3, outer corners round. For single-select, multi-select or
  selection-required choices between **related options**; spans its container
  (cap the width on wide surfaces); one colour style; minimum 48dp per button.
  Don't use one when nothing in it toggles. TASTE §10: two to four exclusive
  options are connected `SelectionGroupButton`s, never a combo box.
- Groups never wrap to a second line; trailing items collapse into an overflow
  menu first. Container not focusable: Tab to the first button, arrows inside.

### 11.5 Split button — no shared widget

Leading button (icon and/or label, 1–2 words) + trailing chevron button, 2dp
apart, inner corners per §7.3, five sizes like buttons. The chevron rotates 180°
on the standard scheme and centres when selected; its colour does not change on
selection (state layer only). Opens a menu aligned to the trailing button, 4dp
away, flipping to whichever edge has room.

### 11.6 FAB, extended FAB, FAB menu — `FloatingActionButton`, `ToolbarPairedFab`

- **FAB:** 56 (radius 16, icon 24) · medium 80 (radius 20, icon 28, the
  recommended default) · large 96 (radius 28, icon 36). Small FAB is retired.
  Colour pairs: primary/secondary/tertiary container (default primary
  container) or the plain accents. Elevation 3, hover 4; 0 when nested in a rail
  or toolbar. Filled icon. One per screen; constructive actions only (create,
  share, start) — never destructive, minor, or overflow. Never disabled (hide
  it). 16dp from the window edges (24 on large windows). Appears by expanding
  from its centre; stays put while content scrolls; disappears and reappears
  across tab switches rather than travelling with content.
- **Extended FAB:** S 56 (radius 16, icon 24, padding 16, gap 8, title medium) ·
  M 80 (radius 20, icon 28, padding 26, gap 12, title large) · L 96 (radius 28,
  icon 36, padding 28, gap 16, headline small). Label required (1–2 words), icon
  optional; hugs content; one per screen; never inside cards or other
  containers, never in the upper half, never with a floating toolbar.
- **FAB menu:** 2–6 related actions opening from a FAB (never from an extended
  FAB); the FAB becomes a 56dp close button in the same place; items are
  medium-button sized, labelled, with icons, hugging content; colour set matches
  the FAB; aligned to the trailing edge; items scroll behind the close button
  when short of room. Not with a toolbar or nav rail on screen.

### 11.7 Toolbars — `Toolbar`, `ToolbarTabBar`, `ToolbarTextField`, `ToolbarPairedFab`

- **Floating toolbar:** 64 tall, fully round, elevation 3 (removable on a
  distinct background), 8dp inner side padding, 4dp between items, ≥16dp from
  the window edge (vertical toolbars ≥24). Holds icon buttons, buttons, text
  fields. Only as big as its items; never past the window edge; overflow menu in
  the trailing slot. No square icon buttons in it (they fight the round
  container); no wide buttons in a vertical one. Can pair with a FAB.
- **Docked toolbar:** full width, square corners, 64 tall, ≥16 side padding,
  items 4–32 apart; bottom only.
- **Standard** colours (surface container) focus attention on the content;
  **vibrant** (primary container) emphasises the controls or signals a mode
  (editing). Emphasise **one** action at most (a filled icon button, a wider
  button, or the paired FAB). Don't show alongside a navigation bar.

### 11.8 Navigation rail — `NavigationRail`, `NavigationRailButton`, `NavigationRailExpandButton`

Collapsed 96 wide (3–7 destinations, never hidden); expanded 220–360 (can show
secondary destinations; standard beside content or modal over it). Items 64 tall,
4 apart; menu button and FAB top-aligned (44dp top space); items top- or
centre-aligned. Active indicator: full-round pill in secondary container, icon
on secondary container and filled, label secondary; the indicator hugs content
in the expanded rail but **the target spans the full rail width**. Labels one
word, never truncated, never shrunk; label medium (horizontal item label large).
Selection uses a top-level transition (§3.3); the indicator expands from the
icon's centre. Never horizontal. One active item.

### 11.9 Tabs — `SecondaryTabBar`, `ToolbarTabBar`

Primary tabs (under a title) or secondary (within content). 48 tall (64 with
icon + label); icon 24; inline icon–label gap 8; active indicator 3dp (primary)
or 2dp (secondary), top corners 3, inset 2dp, ≥24dp long. Labels title small,
short, one row. Related content only, never sequential steps. ≤4 fixed tabs
(scroll beyond; offset the first scrollable tab 52dp). Lateral transition.
Arrows move between tabs; Space/Enter activates.

### 11.10 Cards — `colLayerN` rectangles, `ContentGroup` cards

Elevated (surface container low, level 1), filled (surface container highest),
outlined (surface + outline variant). Radius **12** (medium), side padding 16,
**≤8dp between cards**. A card is either **directly actionable** (one big target,
ripple, no buttons inside) or **a container of actions** (no hover, no ripple of
its own) — never an action on an actionable surface. One swipe action at most.
Drag lifts its elevation. On desktop, card content may scroll; on mobile it
expands instead. Don't force content into cards when spacing and headings would
do. Text on images needs a scrim or a bounding shape.

### 11.11 Lists (expressive) — `StyledListView`, `DialogListItem`, `ContentGroup` runs, `Config*` rows

Rows 56 / 72 / 88 (one / two / three lines; the tallest element decides);
leading and trailing padding 16, element gap 12, top/bottom 10; icons 24. Label
body large, supporting body medium (1–3 lines), trailing text label small.
Middle-aligned, top-aligned from 88 or three lines. **Segmented** style: items
as separate shapes with 2dp gaps, outer corners 16, inner 4 (the shell's
run-ends/seams, DESIGN 5.6). Hover → 12, selected/pressed/focused/dragged → 16.
Selected: the whole item shows it, plus a second cue (checkbox, radio, icon).
One selection mode per list: single-action, multi-action (primary action takes
most of the width, extras trailing), single-select (radios), multi-select
(checkboxes or switches) — one selection control per item. Gaps for contained
lists; dividers only for uncontained ones (not here). Keep elements in the same
position on every row; leading visuals anchored at the leading edge.

### 11.12 Menus (expressive vertical) — `ArrowPopupMotion` popups, `DockFolderPopup`, `DesktopMenu`, `StyledComboBox`

Container radius 16, elevation **2**. Item 44 tall, 16 side padding, 12 between
icon and text, 8 top/bottom; icons 20; label large, supporting body small. Items
4dp radius, first/last outer corners 12, selected 12; groups separated by a 2dp
gap (one or two per menu; none in a scrolling menu). **Standard** colours:
surface container low; selected tertiary container / on tertiary container.
**Vibrant:** tertiary container; selected tertiary / on tertiary — sparingly.
Selected items carry a second cue (checkmark). Opens next to or over its
trigger, flipping to stay on screen; submenus beside the parent item without
overlapping it. Initial focus on the first item; arrows move, Left/Right
open/close submenus, letters jump, Escape closes. Disabled items stay (and
focus). No buttons or switches inside items. The opening control stays visually
the same plus a pressed state.

### 11.13 Dialogs — `WindowDialog`, `WindowDialogTitle`, `WindowDialogParagraph`, `WindowDialogButtonRow`, `DialogButton`

Basic dialog: radius 28, elevation 3, width 280–560, padding 24, 16 between
title and body, 24 between body and actions, 8 between buttons; icon 24 (then
centred); headline small title, body medium text. Over a scrim. **At most two
actions**: a single one only as acknowledgement; otherwise a confirming and a
dismissing action, confirming on the trailing edge, dismissive to its left;
text buttons. No third "Learn more". Headline: a specific statement or question
— no apologies, no "Warning!", no "Are you sure?". Title and buttons stay pinned
when the body scrolls. Errors about fields inline; general failures after a
confirm. Initial focus on the first interactive element, Tab cycles, Escape
closes. Only for high-priority interruptions — low priority goes in a snackbar
or inline. On desktop it may be positioned off-centre, 56dp from the edges.

### 11.14 Side sheets — the sidebars

Standard (beside content, shrinking it) or modal (over a scrim). Max width 400
in M3 (the shell's sidebars are wider by design, `Appearance.sizes.sidebarWidth`),
padding 24, 12 between top elements, 16dp margin when detached, radius 16 on the
free edge (modal). Always a close affordance. Scrolls vertically on its own;
never horizontally. Enters from its edge; exits temporarily (§3.2: emphasized).

### 11.15 Chips — no shared widget (`HermesAttachmentChips` is one instance)

32 tall, radius 8, icon 18, side padding 16 (8 with an icon), 8 between
elements and **≥8 between chips**. Label large, ≤20 characters. Kinds: assist
(smart actions, start with a verb), filter (nouns; selected shows a leading
checkmark), input (user-entered, removable), suggestion (generated replies).
Chips come in sets, never alone; they are contextual, not the way to finish a
task (that is a button). Flat with an outline-variant edge (outline where
interactivity must be obvious); elevated only over imagery; pressed is a ripple,
not elevation. All chip sets on a page are either single- or multi-select. Wrap
to two rows, then scroll horizontally. Remove icons need their own 48 target
(chip ≥88 wide).

### 11.16 Search — `modules/ii/overview/SearchBar.qml`

Bar 56 tall, width 360–720, full radius, surface container high; side margins
24, 12 when focused (it widens). Leading: a navigation button or a non-functional
search icon; ≤2 trailing icons (or one + an avatar). Hint says what is searched
("Search apps"). Results are a list (§11.11) under the bar, grouped by gaps, in
a docked (desktop) or full-screen (compact) layout; input text stays visible
when results show. Back/Escape releases focus. Results are announced.

### 11.17 Text fields — `MaterialTextField` (outlined), `StyledTextInput`, `MaterialTextArea`, `ToolbarTextField`

56 tall, side padding 16 (12 with icons), 16 between icon and text, supporting
text 4 below; filled has extra-small top corners only, outlined is round all
over. Input body large; label body large, floating to body small. Every field
has a label (or an adjacent one), always visible, never truncated; required
fields carry an asterisk explained once. Error text **replaces** supporting text
(so the layout doesn't jump) and says how to fix it, with an error icon. Don't
mix filled and outlined in one region; don't stretch fields across a wide
surface. Clear icon only when there is text.

### 11.18 Switch — `StyledSwitch`, `ConfigSwitch`

Track 52×32, full radius, 2dp outline when off. Handle 16 off, 24 on (or with
an icon), 28 pressed; icons 16 (a check / an X, never ambiguous). State layer 40,
target 48. On: primary track, on primary handle; off: surface container highest
track, outline handle and edge. Takes effect immediately — never for choices that
need Save (use checkboxes). Binary on/off only; opposing options (list vs grid)
are a connected button group. Always an inline label describing what "on"
does, in on surface. Focus lands on the handle; Space/Enter toggles.

### 11.19 Sliders — `StyledSlider`, `StyledVerticalSlider`, `ConfigSlider`

Standard, centred (zero in the middle) and range. Sizes by track height: XS 16
(default), S 24, M 40, L 56, XL 96; track radius 8/8/12/16/28; handle 4 wide,
44 tall (spec table: 52/68/108 for M/L/XL), 6dp clear of the track; inset icon only on M+
standard sliders. Active track primary, inactive secondary container; stop
indicators 4dp, and a stop at the inactive end for 3:1 contrast. The handle
narrows while pressed; the value label appears then. Takes effect immediately.
XL only for hero moments. Arrows step, Space+arrows step larger, Home/End.

### 11.20 Checkbox and radio — `StyledRadioButton` (no shared checkbox)

Checkbox 18 box, radius 2, state layer 40, target 48; parent checkboxes go
indeterminate when some children are checked. Radio icon 20, state layer 40,
target 48; ≤5 options, stacked vertically, one pre-selected, never nested.
Clicking the label selects. Adjacent label in on surface.

### 11.21 Progress and loading — `StyledProgressBar`, `ClippedProgressBar`, `CircularProgress`, `StyledIndeterminateProgressBar`, `MaterialLoadingIndicator`

By expected wait: **under 200ms nothing; 200ms–5s a loading indicator; over 5s
a progress indicator.** Indeterminate → determinate as soon as progress is
known; a loading indicator never turns into a progress bar.
- **Progress:** 4dp track and indicator (thick variant 8), 4dp gap between
  them, full-round ends; wavy option (circular amplitude 1.6, wavelength 15);
  linear 4dp stop dot at the end when contrast needs it; circular 40 (thick 52),
  24–240 range. Primary indicator on secondary container track. One indicator
  for a group, not one per item; same variant for the same process everywhere;
  linear on a container's (animating) edge, circular centred where content will
  appear. In a button: flat, the label's colour, no track.
- **Loading indicator:** 48 container, 38 shape, 24–240 range; primary, or on
  primary container inside a primary-container circle when it sits over
  content (and in pull-to-refresh). Centred in the space content will fill.

### 11.22 Tooltips — `StyledToolTip`, `PopupToolTip`, `StyledToolTipContent`

Plain: inverse surface, 24 tall, 8 padding, body small, one line, a brief label
for an icon-only control; above its target, **4dp** away from a bounded element
or 8dp from text (below if the target is in a top bar). Rich: surface container,
padding 12/16/8, optional title-small subhead and up to two text buttons, placed
bottom-right of the target, shifting in 8dp steps to stay on screen. Hover (or
focus) shows them; they leave 1.5s after the pointer does (§1.2.4); one at a
time; never critical information. Not needed when the control already has a
visible label.

### 11.23 Snackbar — the shell's toasts (`ClipboardToast`) and corner cards

Inverse surface, inverse on surface text, inverse primary action; 48–64 tall
(one or two lines), body medium, opaque. One at a time; a newer one replaces an
outdated one; never stacked. At most one text action (Undo); no icons, links or
filled buttons; no dismiss action needed. Without an action: auto-dismiss in
4–10s, and the information also appears inline; with an action: stays until
acted on. Above FABs, never over navigation; doesn't take focus, doesn't trap
it; announced politely. Nothing else animates with it.

### 11.24 Badges — no shared widget (`ExtensionBadge` is one instance)

Small: 6dp dot. Large: 16 tall, full radius, label small, ≤4 characters ("999+").
Error / on error. Anchored at the icon's top trailing corner (small 6×6 in, large
14×12), never over the icon, never repositioned arbitrarily. Disappears once the
destination is visited.

### 11.25 Carousel — `Carousel`

Layouts: multi-browse (large + medium + small items, snap), uncontained (one
size, free scroll), hero (one large + small preview, snap), centred hero,
full-screen. Item radius 28, padding 16 sides / 8 top-bottom, 8 between items,
small items 40–56 wide. Items resize and parallax as they move. ≤3 items with
text at compact widths. Needs a "Show all" (or a header arrow) so every item is
reachable without horizontal scrolling. Reduced motion: no parallax, equal sizes.
Tab to the first item, arrows between.

### 11.26 Divider

M3: outline variant, 1dp, full-width between unrelated sections or inset within
related ones, "only if items can't be grouped with open space". **This shell
uses none** (§1.1).

### 11.27 Not used in this shell

App bars (headline title large/headline medium/display small; square corners;
fill on scroll), navigation bar (compact windows only), navigation drawer
(replaced by the expanded rail), bottom sheets (compact windows), date and time
pickers (`CalendarView` is the shell's calendar; modal pickers are dialogs at
elevation 3, radius 28). The cache (§14) has their full specs.

---

## 12. Writing

M3's content-design rules, beside TASTE §8:

- **Sentence case** everywhere: buttons, titles, menus, tabs. No title case, no
  caps blocks.
- **Second person** ("your files"); don't mix "my" and "your" on one screen; avoid
  "I"/"we".
- **Short and scannable.** Buttons 1–3 words; FAB/nav labels 1–2; chips ≤20
  characters; badge ≤4.
- **No period** on a single-line sentence; use contractions; serial commas.
- **Ellipses only for an action in progress** ("Connecting…"), never in buttons
  or menu items.
- **Exclamation marks** only for real accomplishments, never empty states.
- **No colons in headings**; parentheses only to define a term.
- **Explain consequences** before an irreversible action and how to undo it.
- **Errors** say what happened and how to fix it, in place, all at once.
- **Accessibility labels** describe the purpose, not the picture ("Voice search",
  not "microphone"), and never include the role ("button").
- Alt text ≤125 characters, no "image of".

---

## 13. Accessibility checklist

- [ ] Text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large); clustered controls 3:1 against the background.
- [ ] Selection, errors and state shown by two cues, never colour alone.
- [ ] Targets 48 touch / 44 pointer (32/40 here), 8 apart.
- [ ] Everything reachable by keyboard: Tab between, arrows within, Space/Enter, Escape.
- [ ] Initial focus defined; focus returns to the opener; nothing traps focus.
- [ ] Every drag/swipe has a single-pointer alternative.
- [ ] Icon-only controls labelled by action, with a tooltip.
- [ ] Text survives 200%: wraps or reflows, padding unchanged, nothing clipped
      without a way to read it.
- [ ] Reduced motion: fades, no parallax, no shape morph.
- [ ] Announcements for changing content (results, snackbars) are polite.

---

## 14. Refreshing this file

`python3 tools/m3-docs.py` reads the site's current version from its app bundle
and mirrors it once per version (`--force` refetches). When the version changes,
diff the token files against the previous version's directory for spec changes,
then update this file and DESIGN.md:

```sh
cd ~/.cache/m3-docs && diff -r <old-version>/tokens <new-version>/tokens
```

`tools/check-m3-tokens.py` asserts that the curves and springs `Appearance` and
`general.lua` carry still match the numbers in §3.
